title: Canceled HTTP/2 requests repeatedly reuse an unresponsive connection
provenance: Evaluator-authored problem-only adaptation of the public upstream issue and observable transport compatibility requirements, retrieved 2026-10-07. Not an authenticated pre-fix issue snapshot. Solution code, reference tests and implementation suggestions omitted. Public historical evaluation case; not a private or contamination-free holdout.
body:
An x/net/http2 client sends requests over a pooled connection. When the peer becomes unresponsive but the underlying connection remains open and writable, request contexts time out or are canceled. Subsequent requests repeatedly choose that same connection and also fail. Closing idle connections after a timeout is not dependable because stream cleanup may still be in progress when the caller tries it.

Fix the transport's handling of canceled requests so an unresponsive connection cannot absorb an unlimited sequence of requests. Preserve the peer's advertised concurrency limit, including stream reservations and canceled streams whose disposition has not been confirmed. Cancellation includes context cancellation after response HEADERS without END_STREAM and Response.Body.Close before stream completion. Earlier response headers do not confirm that the peer processed a later reset. With the ordinary non-strict pool policy, a connection that has exhausted its usable capacity must allow a subsequent request to establish and successfully use a replacement. With StrictMaxConcurrentStreams enabled, pending requests must wait for capacity instead of exceeding the existing connection's advertised limit.

A responsive peer must recover usable capacity and keep a healthy pooled connection reusable across repeated cancellations and ordinary successful requests. Protocol health acknowledgments must release the appropriate waiting capacity, while an ordinary peer-initiated PING must retain its normal request/acknowledgment meaning. Multiple related cancellations must not cause an unbounded stream of duplicate probes, and a later cancellation must still be able to establish fresh health confirmation. Keep public ClientConn state and reservation accounting consistent with actual admission.

Preserve cancellation errors, normal HTTP/2 responses, and connection-close/single-use behavior. A connection already designated non-reusable should not acquire unnecessary health-probe work. Do not solve this by forcing every canceled healthy connection to close, increasing concurrency limits, disabling pooling, or relying on a new global timeout setting.

Add your own native Go regression tests that reproduce the unresponsive-peer behavior and protect healthy cancellation/reuse, strict admission, reservations and replacement. Tests should be deterministic and bounded, use an in-process scripted peer rather than an internet host or firewall command, and preserve the existing HTTP/2 and HPACK tests. The evaluator's private checks are not supplied as candidate tests. Runtime: Go 1.25.5 with GOTOOLCHAIN=local and the repository's pinned module dependencies; dependency access is offline during the task. Native validation command: go test ./http2 ./http2/hpack -count=1 -timeout=120s -parallel=2.
